relevance_note: The paper gives individual-level detail (age 37, male, died of SUDEP) for one in-scope person, 'a 37 y.o. male patient with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (SSADHD)'.
method_note: Read the full Markdown by hand; no script transcribed any table, so every span was copied manually and re-checked against the file. Scope: only the single SSADHD patient is described individually. The four control subjects (8 control autopsies) are out of scope and get no rows, and the patient's 'family' is mentioned only collectively ('The family ofthe patient consented both to autopsy...') with no individual-level facts, so no relative rows were created. No ALDH5A1 variant or mutation is printed for the patient anywhere (the paper gives only the diagnosis), so the variants table is empty; no variant description was filled from memory. Only one clinical feature is explicitly reported for the patient (SUDEP); the numerous post-mortem tissue metabolite findings (e.g. elevated total GABA/GHB) are biochemical measurements, not clinical features, and were not entered in phenotypic_features. Checklist item 'seizures or epilepsy' was set to observed because the paper states the patient 'expired from SUDEP (sudden unexpected death of epilepsy)' and the Table 1 legend defines SUDEP as 'sudden unexplained death in epilepsy'. Contradictions found in the paper: (1) SUDEP is written 'sudden unexpected death of epilepsy' in the text but 'sudden unexplained death in epilepsy' in the Table 1 legend; (2) GABA is 'within the range of control values' in the Results but the Discussion describes 'glutamine/GABA (elevated)' in patient cortical sections. Tables 1 and 2 are specimen/matrix tables; Table 2 carries only matrix-level references (Brown et al. in press; Brown et al. 2019; Jansen et al. 2016; Current report) describing group data, so no source_reference_in_review values were taken from them. Age at diagnosis and the basis of diagnosis are not stated for the patient; the 1985 date refers to the earlier publication, not to the diagnosis.
